title: Rule Lab: a fix must keep its counterexample
audience: Teams that need quality rules to be explainable, testable, and safe to change.
promise: Start from a finding, edit an isolated rule, compare positive and negative fixtures, and save a receipt bound to the target and engine.
story: A concrete finding names the rule, risk, and fixture that motivated the edit.
A canonical rule and an isolated draft run against the same positive and negative suite.
The comparison shows no gained or lost matches, preserving the counterexample.
A fresh receipt records the target revision, engine version, and bounded result.
verified_locally: Current dev branch is clean at bcddbe0f7615d654c9d0866c603955e67db380e5; pytest, Ruff, and extension tests pass.
Canonical and draft rules compared against positive and negative fixtures.
Gained and lost matches are empty and the counterexample remains intact.
Receipt saved locally and re-checked as fresh against the fixture target.
A crop-safe 1600x900 SVG/PNG preview is visually inspected.
open_gates: Move a receipt through the Quality Lens and Evidence Replay producer seam.
Capture direct VS Code acceptance with the same rule, fixture, and result.
Add stale and malformed scenario captures to the public evidence matrix.
Resolve the eight current pyright type errors or record an accepted typecheck boundary.
Record external GitHub, portfolio, and Handshake readbacks.
claim_boundary: This packet proves the current dev W2 headless fixture-comparison slice and fresh local receipt; it does not claim IDE parity, cross-producer acceptance, universal type health, automatic repair, hosting, or publication.
